sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell a house in Lockport?
sections.html:
Lockport owners can list through an agent, sell by owner, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases the house in its current condition. One local detail simplifies the money side: the city's own FAQ says Lockport does not impose a transfer tax, so the taxes at closing come from the state and the county, not the city.

Lockport is in Will County, so the deed goes to the Will County Recorder of Deeds in Joliet, and property tax questions go to the Will County Treasurer and Supervisor of Assessments.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Lockport?
sections.html:
Lockport sits on the east bank of the Des Plaines River just north of Joliet, with the village of Lemont about two miles north. The 2020 census counted 26,094 residents, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate of 27,822 is 6.6 percent above the 2020 estimates base, the only one of the four Illinois places in this Census comparison that gained population.

The city grew around the Illinois and Michigan Canal. The original canal headquarters building from 1837 now holds a museum, the Gaylord Building (1838, local limestone) holds a restaurant and galleries, and the Norton Building (1850, built as a grain processor) houses lofts, offices and a state museum gallery. The Gladys Fox Museum sits in an 1839 church, and Lincoln Landing is an open-air park beside the canal. The city also has a Historic Preservation District with its own permit rules, which affects what an owner there can change.

sections.h2: Which Lockport schools and districts matter to buyers?
sections.html:
All of Lockport falls in Lockport Township High School District 205, whose Central Campus (opened 1910) serves freshmen and whose East Campus (opened 1964) serves sophomores through seniors. The grade-school pattern is more fragmented, and the district tied to a street can change a buyer's interest.

  • Taft School District 90 covers the southwest part of the city.
  • Milne-Kelvin Grove District 91 covers the west central part, with Milne Grove for kindergarten through grade 3 and Kelvin Grove for grades 4 to 8.
  • Will County School District 92 serves the north, with Walsh, Reed, Ludwig and Oak Prairie schools.
  • Homer District 33C serves the east and Fairmont District 89 serves the south.

Catholic options include Saints Dennis and Joseph Catholic Academy in the city, plus Providence Catholic in New Lenox and Joliet Catholic Academy nearby.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Lockport homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists Lockport as an owner-heavy city with a large share of college graduates and long commutes.

The 35.3-minute average commute is the longest of the four comparison places on the same Census table. Commuters have alternatives: Lockport has a Metra Heritage Corridor station with weekday rush-hour service to Chicago Union Station, Pace routes 832 and 834 reach Joliet, and Interstate 355 runs through the area.

sections.h2: Which Lockport permits and rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
Most of the pre-listing questions are answered by the city's Building Department FAQ. Over-the-counter permits cover HVAC, water heaters, roofs, siding and windows, and other work goes through plan review that typically takes 10 to 14 business days when the submission is complete. A remodeling permit stays valid six months, and a new building permit one year.

  • Contractors working in the city must register with the Building Department before starting, and work hours are 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Saturday and 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Sunday.
  • Owners may do their own work on an owner-occupied single-family home, but the city does not allow house flipping unless every tradesperson registers.
  • A swimming pool 24 inches or deeper needs a permit and a four-foot barrier with a self-closing, self-locking gate.
  • Changes inside the Historic District need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Planning Department.

The FAQ also covers the plat of survey: look in your closing papers first, since the city usually holds a plat only for homes built since 2002. A new survey costs about $500 by the city's estimate.

sections.h2: What is the landlord program and who does it affect?
sections.html:
If the house has been rented, the Code Enforcement Department runs a landlord rental property registration with health and life safety inspections. Its duties also include abandoned vehicles, grass over 8 inches, exterior maintenance on dilapidated buildings, pool barrier violations and signs without permits.

An investor buying a Lockport rental should ask the department how the registration transfers, and a seller moving out of a former rental should ask whether the property is registered. Code Enforcement answers at 815-838-0549, extension 2153 for the assistant line.

sections.h2: How do roads, parks and flood maps shape a Lockport listing?
sections.html:
Buyers ask who plows and repairs the street. In Lockport the answer varies: the Illinois Department of Transportation maintains Route 7 (9th Street and 159th Street), Route 53 (Broadway), Route 171 (State Street and Archer Avenue) and New Avenue, Will County maintains roads such as 143rd Street, Briggs Street and Cedar Road, and the city maintains streets including Farrell Road and Division Street west of Briggs.

Parks add to the pitch. The Lockport Township Park District, created in 1945, manages 38 parks, and Dellwood Park hosts October haunted attractions. For flood risk, the city points owners to FEMA's Flood Map Service Center and its Engineering Department, because a floodplain location can change building requirements and insurance needs. Pull the map for your parcel before you list, and note that a private-line sewer or water repair stays with the owner while main-line problems belong to the city.

sections.h2: How do water, trash and snow rules work at closing?
sections.html:
The city lets sellers order a final water reading by calling the Water Department at 815-838-0549, option 3, with the closing date, a forwarding address for the final bill and the purchaser's name. Water and garbage bills mail around the first of the month and are due by the 15th.

Trash and recycling run through an inclusive city contract with Waste Management, with yard waste collected from April 1 through the first week of December. For winter, the city maintains 108 miles of roadway with 11 snowplow trucks and aims to clear streets within 24 hours after snow stops. Parking on city streets is banned when snowfall exceeds 2 inches, and curb parking is barred from 3 to 6 a.m. The city replaced vehicle stickers in 2015 with a municipal electric excise tax, so a buyer has no sticker to purchase.

On the private side, the homeowner owns the sewer line from the house to the main, and a home with a sprinkler system needs an annual backflow (RPZ) test report before the system is turned on each season.

sections.h2: What happens with recording and tax in Will County?
sections.html:
Recording happens at the Will County Recorder of Deeds in Joliet (815-740-4637 on the county directory), and the Illinois transfer declaration and 50-cent-per-$500 state tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-10 still apply even though Lockport adds nothing. Property tax bills come from the Will County Treasurer, and the Treasurer's page explains that delinquent taxes can be sold at the annual tax sale, with homeowners typically getting one to three years to redeem. Ask the treasurer about current balances before you set a closing date.

A cash buyer in Lockport should confirm who pays recording fees and whether any unpaid city water or code fines must be cleared first.

faqs.q: Does Lockport charge a city transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. The city's FAQ says Lockport does not impose a transfer tax. The state tax of 50 cents per $500 under 35 ILCS 200/31-10 still applies to the sale.

faqs.q: How do I order a final water reading?
faqs.a: Call the city Water Department at 815-838-0549, option 3, with the closing date, the address for the final bill and the purchaser's name. Bills mail around the first of the month and are due by the 15th.

faqs.q: Can I do my own repairs before selling?
faqs.a: Yes, if you own and live in a single-family home, though permits are still required and the city bars house flipping unless all trades register. Painting, tuckpointing and fixture swaps need no permit outside the Historic District.

faqs.q: Which school district covers my Lockport address?
faqs.a: Every address is in Lockport Township High School District 205. Grade school depends on the street: Taft 90, Milne-Kelvin Grove 91, Will County 92, Homer 33C or Fairmont 89. Confirm with the district before listing.

faqs.q: Is a historic district permit different?
faqs.a: Yes. Changes within the Historic District go through the Certificate of Appropriateness process with the Planning Department, and the list of exempt ordinary repairs does not apply there.
